rules.desc: Students should complete a minimum of 10 units from the courses listed below. Departmental courses may fulfill the requirements for more than one emphasis. You will work with your faculty advisor to select emphasis courses related to a plan of study with a specific focus on a theoretical and/or geographical area.

rules.name: Anthropology Elective Coursework (20 units)
rules.desc:
The remainder of the 30 required units may be fulfilled with any Anthropology courses, or a combination of Anthropology courses and up to successfully petitioned 10 units from related areas of study, overseas studies, and/or transfer units.
No more than 5 units of directed reading-style/ research coursework listed may be counted toward the minor.

rules.name: Overall grade of C or higher in the minor coursework
C or better in two ANTHRO essential courses at the 100 level or higher, taught by Anthropology faculty
Faculty advisor in Anthropology, declared by the penultimate quarter, two quarters in the minor

gpa: A minimum overall grade of 'C' or higher in minor coursework is required.
grading:
A program of 30 units, with a minimum grade of ‘C’ or higher. Of the 30 units:

• At least 10 units must be taken from the chosen ANTHRO emphasis

• At least 15 units must be ANTHRO courses numbered 100 or above.

• No more than 5 units must be Directed Reading-style coursework may be counted towards the minor.

• No more than 5 units may be taken for a satisfactory / no credit grade

• A grade of ‘C’ or higher in two ANTHRO essential courses listed at the 100 level or higher and taught by Anthro faculty
policies:
• A faculty advisor appointed in the Department of Anthropology is required for the minor.

• At least two quarters of enrollment is needed in the minor. Each candidate for the minor in Anthropology should declare no later than the first day of the penultimate quarter before degree conferral.
transferPolicy:
No more than 10 units may be approved from related areas of study, overseas studies, and transfer units.
Note: Any related overseas studies or transfer units must be approved by the faculty advisor and by petition to the Undergraduate Committee. Submit a faculty advisor-approved Undergraduate Course Exception Form found on the department website to the Undergraduate Student Services Officer for final review by the Undergraduate Committee.
reviewNotes: The audit checks 10 units from one emphasis list (Cultural & Social, Environmental or Medical) and 20 more units of ANTHRO courses, with at most 5 units of directed reading or research, toward the 30 units the minor needs. Every course needs a C or better; at least 15 units must be ANTHRO courses numbered 100 or above, at most 5 units may be S/NC, and at least 20 units must be ANTHRO, since at most 10 may come from related areas, overseas study or transfer. Approved department courses off an emphasis list, a self-designed emphasis and petitioned outside units are moved in by hand. You check by hand the C average, the two essential ANTHRO courses, and your faculty advisor and declaration.
